interpolant_reproduction.statement: IntakeSurface interpolates with scipy LinearNDInterpolator(rescale=True): points rescaled to (p - mean) / ptp, Delaunay triangulation by Qhull ('Qbb Qc Qz Q12' + 'Qt'), linear (barycentric) interpolation in the containing simplex. The v1 grid is a full tensor product (4 x 2 x 5 x 3), so the Delaunay problem is degenerate: every grid cell has 16 cospherical corners and the interpolant depends on the simplices Qhull returns (830 simplices, 259 of them degenerate and never selected, 571 non-degenerate, each inside one grid cell; any other triangulation, or multilinear interpolation, differs by up to about 10 % in CR_passive). The Rust surface therefore does not re-triangulate: it reads the reference's own triangulation, captured from the reference environment by scripts/rust_migration/capture_intake_surface_triangulation.py into crates/abep-intake/data/intake_surface_v1_delaunay_v1.json (sha256 247601cf51cff450759a2148179242e8085eb8fb0b878d87e44ea86e644faf7b; 30 interpolators (2 scattering x 3 species x 5 columns) checked identical at capture), hash-pinned in the crate.
interpolant_reproduction.rust_load_checks: on load the Rust surface (a) verifies the capture sha256 and the frozen CSV / JSON sha256, (b) checks that every (scattering, species) table lists the captured 120 points in the captured order, (c) recomputes offset (sequential row sum / 120) and scale (max - min) and requires them bitwise equal to the captured values, (d) checks that every non-degenerate simplex lies in one grid cell and that the non-degenerate simplices of each cell have integer index-space volumes |det| summing to 4! (exact tiling), and that every degenerate simplex has index-space volume 0. Any failure is MODEL_ERROR (fail closed).
interpolant_reproduction.rust_evaluation: query rescaled as (x - offset) / scale; the first non-degenerate simplex (in captured order) whose barycentric coordinates all lie in [-eps, 1 + eps], eps = 100 DBL_EPSILON (scipy's eps), is used; barycentric coordinates c_i = sum_j Tinv[i][j] (x_j - r_j), c_4 = 1 - sum c_i, with r = vertex 4 and Tinv from Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting of T[i][j] = p[s_j][i] - r[i] (scipy uses LAPACK; differences are rounding only); value = sum_k c_k v[s_k] in vertex order starting from 0. Scipy selects among simplices containing a boundary point by its own walk; values on shared faces agree up to rounding. No containing simplex -> OUT_OF_DOMAIN (Python: NaN -> _row refuses).
interpolant_reproduction.why_this_is_not_a_synthetic_reference: the capture is the reference implementation's own internal structure over the frozen data, not a reference output; reference values are never captured into the Rust implementation

E4_IntakeSurface.tolerance_basis: r_rel 1e-11 (not the template's 1e-12) because the barycentric coordinates are computed from a different LU of the same simplex matrix: over the 571 non-degenerate reference simplices the 2-norm condition number is at most 42.8 (median 12.2), so coordinate errors are <= ~2e-14 and value errors <= ~5e-13 relative before the species recombination (ratios of positive terms); 1e-11 keeps a 20x margin. A wrong simplex, a different triangulation or a wrong recombination gives relative differences of 1e-4 .. 1e-1, so the bound loses no detection power. The pandas parse deviation (DIV-05) is 1 ulp of a node value

list.name: v2 status label and primary blocker

tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, error codes, schema shape: equal
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: |rust - py| <= k_ulp ulp(py) OR <= r_rel * max(1, |py|); k_ulp and r_rel per observable above
tolerance_classes.STATISTICAL: per test |mean_rust - mean_py| <= z * sqrt(se_py^2 + se_rust^2), z = 5.0 (Kernel-1 value); zero-se rule |diff| <= 1e-12 * max(1, |mean_py|) when se_py = se_rust = 0; aggregate |sum z_i| / sqrt(N) <= 4.0 per entry point and observable over the vectors with nonzero combined se (Kernel-1 value)
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: NOT_APPLICABLE (A9.29 sec. 7: never applied to the TPMC kernel)

statistical_basis: E1: 53 vectors x 8 statistical observables = 424 tests; with 16 replicates per side the z statistic has about 30 degrees of freedom and P(|t_30| > 5) is about 2e-5, so the expected number of false rejections is about 0.01. E2: 11 binomial tests, normal tail at 5 is 5.7e-7. Aggregate |sum z| / sqrt(N) <= 4: about 6e-5 per observable under the null

domain_and_error_parity.message_key_rule: Python messages are classified by registered substrings: 'unknown wall-scattering model' -> UNKNOWN_SCATTERING; 'must be finite and inside [0, 1]' or 'must be a finite real number in [0, 1]' -> ACCOMMODATION_INVALID; 'intake ROM extrapolation' -> OUT_OF_BOUNDS; 'needs explicit free-stream mass fractions' -> FRACTIONS_REQUIRED; 'mass fractions must be finite and >= 0' -> FRACTION_INVALID; 'are not in the frozen table' -> FOREIGN_SPECIES; 'all mass fractions are zero' -> ALL_ZERO; 'non-finite' -> NON_FINITE_ROW; 'needs m_mean_build_kg' -> M_MEAN_BUILD_REQUIRED; KeyError -> UNKNOWN_SPECIES; IntakeSurfaceV2Blocked -> V2_BLOCKED. Rust messages start with the key followed by ': '
domain_and_error_parity.mapping_rule: every Python exception class / status used by the component maps to exactly one Rust error variant / status: ValueError and KeyError -> AbepError::OutOfDomain (status OUT_OF_DOMAIN) with the registered message key; IntakeSurfaceV2Blocked -> EvalStatus::NotEvaluated; non-convergence (converged False, returned not raised) -> returned record with converged false (Rust status MODEL_ERROR, INV-09). No Rust path returns a value where Python fails or fails where Python returns, except the documented divergences (CLAUDE.md rule 3: no silent fallbacks)

decision_rules.per_test: every scored observable meets its tolerance class
decision_rules.aggregate: STATISTICAL entry points E1 and E2: |sum_i z_i| / sqrt(N) <= 4.0 per observable over the vectors with nonzero combined se
decision_rules.entry_point_result: PARITY_PASS or PARITY_FAIL per entry point E1..E5: PARITY_PASS iff all its per-test, aggregate, invariant, conservation, domain / error and schema checks pass
decision_rules.verdict: ADMITTED iff every entry point is PARITY_PASS, every required invariant holds, and every reference file and pinned input matches its registered sha256; otherwise NOT_ADMITTED (or REFUSED_REFERENCE_CHANGED / INPUT_MISMATCH / NOT_RUN_RUST_UNAVAILABLE)
decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: A9.24 item 1: Rust becomes authoritative for intake_response, response_surface, clausing_transmission and the frozen v1 IntakeSurface (within the registered domain); new production results for them come from Rust and carry implementation = rust, rust_commit and this contract id; the Python functions may then be retired from active execution. It is NOT physics validation, and it does not rebuild or replace intake_surface_v1
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
decision_rules.disagreement_rule: never rewrite a Python result, golden, fixture or frozen dataset to make Rust pass (RM-R11)
decision_rules.observable_scope: observables are restricted to retained selected-architecture physics; an observable that depends on an excluded legacy path is not registered (RM-R20)
